steps: Like parallel forces are parallel forces that act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces are parallel forces that act in opposite directions.
items.finalAnswer: Like parallel forces act in the same direction; unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

steps: The components of a vector along two mutually perpendicular directions are called its rectangular components.
If a force F makes an angle θ with the x-axis, its rectangular components are:
Horizontal component: Fx = F cos θ.
Vertical component: Fy = F sin θ.
items.finalAnswer: Rectangular components are the mutually perpendicular components of a vector: Fx = F cos θ and Fy = F sin θ, when θ is measured from the x-axis.

steps: The line of action of a force is the straight line along which the force acts.
items.finalAnswer: The line of action is the straight line along which a force acts.

steps: The moment of a force about a point is the product of the force and the perpendicular distance of its line of action from that point.
Let a force F act at a point whose position vector r makes an angle θ with F.
The perpendicular distance d from the point of rotation to the line of action of F is d = r sin θ.
Moment of force, τ = Fd.
Substituting d = r sin θ: τ = F(r sin θ) = rF sin θ.
items.finalAnswer: The moment of a force is τ = rF sin θ.

items.figure: Draw two equal, parallel forces F acting in opposite directions at two points separated by perpendicular distance d. Mark the forces with arrows in opposite directions and label the arrangement a couple.
steps: Draw two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions, with their lines of action separated by a perpendicular distance d.
The resultant force is zero because the two forces are equal and opposite: ΣF = F − F = 0.
Their moments act in the same rotational direction, so the resultant torque is not zero: τ = Fd.
This arrangement is called a couple.
items.finalAnswer: A couple has zero resultant force but a non-zero resultant torque.

items.figure: (a) The cone on its circular base: stable equilibrium. (b) The ball on top of the dome: unstable equilibrium. (c) The cylinder lying on its side: neutral equilibrium.
steps: (a) The cone resting on its circular base is in stable equilibrium.
(b) The ball on top of the dome is in unstable equilibrium.
(c) The cylinder lying on its side is in neutral equilibrium.
items.finalAnswer: (a) Stable equilibrium; (b) unstable equilibrium; (c) neutral equilibrium.

steps: A body moving with constant velocity in a straight line is in dynamic equilibrium because the resultant force acting on it is zero.
For example, a car moving along a straight road with constant velocity is in equilibrium.
items.finalAnswer: A car moving in a straight line with constant velocity is in dynamic equilibrium.

steps: The centre of mass of a body is the point at which the whole mass of the body may be considered to be concentrated.
The centre of gravity of a body is the point through which the whole weight of the body acts.
items.finalAnswer: The centre of mass represents the body's whole mass, while the centre of gravity is the point through which its whole weight acts.
